key_insight: Engine position mainly affects early contrail formation and vortex-regime dynamics, but its impact fades later as wake evolution becomes dominated by vortex physics and atmospheric conditions.
engineering_relevance: Aircraft engine placement can meaningfully change near-field contrail behavior, which matters for wake modeling and contrail mitigation studies during the first stages after emission.
method: 3D Large Eddy Simulations on a realistic aircraft configuration
Coupled Eulerian bulk microphysics model for contrail evolution
Initialized from prior Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes fields to capture near-field jet-vortex interaction and far-field wake dynamics
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparisons across three engine positions under two atmospheric stratifications and two relative humidity conditions, showing early differences in vortex instability and descent but convergence of microphysical contrail properties over time.
watch_item: The conclusions are limited to the specific engine placements, atmospheric stratifications, and humidity conditions tested, so broader generalization may require additional cases.
paper_title: Engine position effects on contrail evolution for a realistic aircraft configuration
